title: Assessment of Clients with Genitourinary Disorders
path: Assessment of Clients with Genitourinary Disorders

headings.title: Introduction to Genitourinary Assessment
headings.content: Assessment of the genitourinary system covers both the urinary tract and the male or female reproductive organs. Nurses in Nigerian clinical settings encounter patients presenting with various complaints, ranging from urinary tract infections to chronic kidney disease. A systematic evaluation helps uncover hidden pathologies and guides prompt nursing interventions. Establishing trust and maintaining patient privacy are paramount because these examinations touch on sensitive body areas. Communication must remain professional, calm, and reassuring throughout the interaction.

headings.title: Health History and Symptom Analysis
headings.content:
Gathering a detailed health history forms the backbone of any genitourinary evaluation. Nurses must inquire about specific urinary symptoms using precise terminology, yet explain concepts simply to the patient. 

- **Dysuria**: Pain or burning sensation during urination, often indicating infection.
- **Hematuria**: Presence of blood in the urine, which can be macroscopic or microscopic.
- **Frequency**: Needing to urinate more often than usual without an increase in total volume.
- **Urgency**: A sudden, compelling need to pass urine that is difficult to delay.
- **Nocturia**: Waking up multiple times at night to void, disrupting normal sleep patterns.

Ask about previous urinary tract infections, sexually transmitted infections, pelvic surgeries, and family history of renal disease. Documenting medications, fluid intake patterns, and known allergies is equally critical.

headings.title: Physical Examination Techniques
headings.content:
Physical assessment of the genitourinary system follows the standard clinical sequence of inspection, palpation, and percussion, though auscultation is occasionally used for renal bruit. 

Inspection begins with the external genitalia and perineal area for rashes, lesions, swelling, or abnormal discharge. Palpation of the urinary bladder occurs over the suprapubic region; a distended bladder feels like a smooth, rounded, tender dome above the symphysis pubis. Costovertebral angle tenderness is checked by gently percussing or fist-percussing the area where the lower ribs meet the spine, which helps identify renal inflammation or pyelonephritis.

headings.title: Diagnostic and Laboratory Investigations
headings.content:
Laboratory tests provide objective data regarding renal function and the presence of urinary tract pathogens. 

| Test | Normal Purpose / Indicator | Clinical Significance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Urinalysis** | Detects cells, casts, protein, and glucose | High leukocytes indicate infection; protein indicates glomerular damage |
| **Urine Culture** | Identifies specific bacteria and sensitivities | Guides appropriate antibiotic selection for treatment |
| **Serum Creatinine** | Measures waste product from muscle breakdown | Elevated levels reflect impaired glomerular filtration rate |
| **Blood Urea Nitrogen** | Measures urea nitrogen in the blood | Rises with renal impairment, dehydration, or high protein intake |

Instructing patients on proper midstream clean-catch urine collection prevents sample contamination from skin flora.

headings.title: Specialized Diagnostic Procedures
headings.content: When basic labs and physical exams prove inconclusive, specialized procedures are ordered. Ultrasound of the kidneys, ureters, and bladder visualizes structural abnormalities, stones, or hydronephrosis without radiation exposure. Cystoscopy involves inserting a slender, lighted scope through the urethra to inspect the bladder lining directly. Nurses must monitor patients closely after cystoscopy for hematuria, dysuria, and signs of urinary retention or infection. Urodynamic studies evaluate bladder storage and emptying efficiency by measuring pressures and flow rates.

headings.title: Documentation and Findings Analysis
headings.content: Accurate documentation ensures continuity of care across multidisciplinary healthcare teams. Nurses record all subjective complaints, objective measurement values, laboratory results, and imaging reports in the patient's record. Analyzing these findings helps identify priority nursing diagnoses such as impaired urinary elimination, acute pain, or risk for infection. Communicating abnormal trends promptly to the physician prevents acute renal failure or worsening sepsis in vulnerable patients.
